bottleneck.description: AI self-driving software stack (Kodiak Driver) for Class-8 trucks and military AGV applications; competitive autonomy-software market with multiple credible peers.

dependency.key_customers: Atlas Energy Solutions, U.S. Department of Defense, General Dynamics Land Systems (partnership), Verizon Business, freight shippers
dependency.key_suppliers: Nvidia (compute), Luminar/sensor vendors, OEM truck chassis providers, AWS/cloud compute

editorial.notes: Kodiak operates in a multi-vendor autonomous-trucking market alongside Aurora (regarded as the leader), Plus (partnered with Traton/Navistar), Waabi, Gatik, and Embark legacy, plus OEM in-house programs. While Kodiak has differentiated wins (Atlas Energy customer-owned trucks, a ~$30M DoD contract, General Dynamics AGV collaboration, Verizon partnership), no single end-user is locked in and substitution paths exist. Its early defense-collaboration footprint and operational maturity are commercial strengths, not a bottleneck. The autonomy-software market is exactly the kind of contested frontier-stack baseline the framework labels LOW.
